title: Durable server-side queue admission on Queue press
goal: When the user presses Queue in OpenChamber, the message must be admitted to OpenCode's durable v2 server queue (POST /api/session/:sessionID/prompt with delivery:'queue') and acknowledged, so the client can be closed/slept immediately and the message still runs. The local Zustand/localStorage queue survives only as an explicitly-labelled fallback for servers that do not support v2 durable admission.
assumptions: Live OpenCode is 1.18.21 and supports POST /api/session/:sessionID/prompt with body {prompt:{text,files,agents}, delivery:'queue'}, returning a SessionInputAdmitted acknowledgement, durable across client disconnect and server restart.
The legacy prompt_async path used today by OpencodeClient.sendMessage (packages/ui/src/lib/opencode/client.ts:896) does NOT accept delivery:'queue'. It must not be reused for admission.
The v2 durable queue exposes no list, edit, cancel, or reorder operation. Admission is one-way and irreversible from the client.

The v2 prompt input carries no per-input model / agent / variant fields. Those are session-level settings resolved by the server at drain time, so the per-item sendConfig captured today (messageQueueStore.ts:49) has no meaning for admitted items.

@opencode-ai/sdk is pinned at 1.18.18 in both package.json and packages/ui/package.json while the live server is 1.18.21, so the SDK may not type delivery:'queue'. A raw runtimeFetch POST is an accepted transport (client.ts already uses runtimeFetch for /api/session-activity, /api/agent, and /fs/*).
Server admission is the only path that lets the client sleep. Any item still held locally must be visibly labelled as requiring the client to stay open.
Queue capacity guards MAX_MESSAGES_PER_QUEUE=20 and MAX_QUEUE_TARGETS=50 apply only to locally-held items; the server owns its own queue depth.

Existing ambiguous-transport-failure tagging in client.ts (markAmbiguousTransportFailure / isAmbiguousTransportFailure) is the correct precedent for never auto-retrying a dispatched-but-unconfirmed write.

tasks.goal: Rewire the Queue press in the composer. handleQueueMessage becomes an async admission: capture the composer snapshot and inline drafts exactly as today, generate the client message id, insert the item in pending-admission state so the chip appears instantly, clear the composer, then attempt admission. On admitted, mark admitted. On unsupported, downgrade the item to local state and leave the existing local drain to handle it. On deterministic failure or ambiguous transport failure, mark admission-failed. Additionally, because the v2 queue has no per-input model/agent/variant, persist the composer's current model/agent/variant to the session selection before admission so the server's session-level config matches the user's intent at Queue time. Finally, exclude admitted and pending-admission items from the whole-queue merge in handleSubmit.

success_criteria: Pressing Queue against OpenCode 1.18.21 issues exactly one POST to /api/session/:sessionID/prompt with delivery:'queue' and the message body, and the chip shows an acknowledged server-queued state.
After acknowledgement, closing or sleeping the OpenChamber client does not prevent the message from running; no client-side drain is required.
No admitted message can be delivered twice via the auto-send drain, the composer whole-queue merge, the chip force-send, or a retry after an ambiguous transport failure.

Against a server without v2 durable queue support, Queue press silently falls back to the existing local queue, the chip is labelled as requiring the client to stay open, and current behaviour is otherwise unchanged.
No queue UI control offers edit, reorder, cancel, or remove on a server-admitted item.
Attachments and agent mentions queued via admission arrive with identical normalization to a direct send.
On any admission failure the user's text is preserved and recoverable to the composer in one action.
bun run type-check:ui, bun run lint:ui, and bun run --cwd packages/ui test all exit 0.
An exact-payload test pins the admission request body key names and endpoint path.

out_of_scope: Phase G non-goal: building any client-side emulation of edit, reorder, cancel, or list for server-admitted items. The v2 API cannot back these operations and faking them creates duplicate or phantom messages.
Phase G non-goal: per-queued-item model, agent, or variant selection. These are session-level in v2; the plan writes the session selection at Queue press instead.
Phase G non-goal: removing the local Zustand queue. It remains the labelled fallback for servers without v2 durable admission.
Phase G non-goal: changing the steer delivery path or the follow-up behaviour setting semantics ('steer' vs 'queue' in messageQueueStore.ts:9-41).
Phase G non-goal: adding a server-side queue depth, priority, or scheduling feature.
Phase G non-goal: bumping @opencode-ai/sdk as part of this change; the raw-fetch transport avoids coupling the feature to a dependency upgrade.
Phase G non-goal: changing the new-session draft send path; admission applies to existing sessions only, since a draft has no session id to admit against.
risk_flags: Wire-contract drift: the SDK pin (1.18.18) trails the live server (1.18.21), so body key names are assumed until T0 confirms them. Mitigation: T0 is blocking and Phase 5 pins the payload with an exact assertion.

Duplicate delivery is the highest-severity failure: four separate code paths can deliver a queued item (auto-send drain, composer whole-queue merge, chip force-send, retry after failure). Mitigation: single chokepoint at getSendableQueue plus an enumerated review in T7.

Irreversibility: admission cannot be undone, so an accidental Queue press is unrecoverable. Mitigation: the pending state is optimistic but short-lived, and the UI must be explicit that server-queued items cannot be edited or cancelled.

Ambiguous transport failure over the relay may leave a message admitted while the client believes it failed; a naive retry would double-deliver. Mitigation: no auto-retry, explicit unknown-outcome state, manual user action only.

Attachment payload size: data-URL attachments in the admission body may exceed proxy or relay limits that the streaming send path tolerates differently. Mitigation: reuse the existing normalization and verify large-attachment admission in T8.

Session-level model/agent semantics change silently: a user who queues with model A and then switches the session to model B will have the queued message run under B. Mitigation: write the selection at Queue press and surface the session-level nature in the chip copy.

Persist migration risk: mismarking a legacy v2 item as admitted would strand it forever with no drain and no server copy. Mitigation: migration maps every legacy item to local state, asserted by test.
Scope creep into a full queue-management UI. Mitigation: Phase G non-goals are explicit and the MVP cut line is Phases 0-5.
